items.title: FAAC shares N2.428trn among FG, states, LGs
items.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has shared N2.428 trillion among the Federal Government, state governments and local government councils as revenue accrued to the Federation Account and proceeds from Value Added Tax (VAT) for September 2026. According to a communiqué issued at the end of the committee’s meeting in Abuja, the amount was higher than the N2.338 trillion shared in the preceding month. The total distributable revenue comprised N1.672 trillion in statutory revenue and N756.587 billion from VAT. The committee disclosed that gross revenue for September stood at N3.913 trillion, out of which N131.758 billion was deducted as the cost of collection, while N1.352 trillion went to transfers, refunds and savings. The communiqué stated that gross statutory revenue of N3.096 trillion was recorded in September, an increase of N246.384 billion over the N2.850 trillion recorded in August. However, gross VAT revenue fell to N816.872 billion in September from N834.843 billion in August, representing a decline of N17.972 billion. Of the N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received N832.242 billion, while state governments received N799.872 billion. Local government councils received N560.660 billion, while N236.049 billion was shared among benefiting states as 13 per cent derivation revenue from mineral resources. A breakdown of the N1.672 trillion distributable statutory revenue showed that the Federal Government received N756.583 billion, state governments got N383.749 billion, and local government councils received N295.855 billion. The benefiting states also received N236.049 billion as derivation revenue. From the N756.587 billion distributable VAT revenue, the Federal Government received N75.659 billion, state governments got N416.123 billion, while local government councils received N264.805 billion. FAAC said revenue from Petroleum Profit Tax, Hydrocarbon Tax, petroleum royalties, import duty, Common External Tariff levies and excise duty increased significantly during the period. However, receipts from Companies Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax, Stamp Duties, VAT, mineral royalties, gas-flaring penalties and fees, and miscellaneous oil revenue declined. items.title: Vol de Renoir en France : une trace ADN permet de retrouver les œuvres dérobées
items.description: Plus d'un mois apres leur disparition, Portrait de Madame Colonna Romano et Jeune femme au puits ont ete retrouves dans une maison de l'Herault. Les deux tableaux etaient dissimules derriere un faux mur. Selon Associated Press, les enqueteurs ont reussi a remonter jusqu'aux suspects en exploitant une trace ADN et les donnees de geolocalisation d'un vehicule. Une alarme qui precipite la fuite des voleurs Le vol remonte au 8 septembre . Deux individus s'etaient introduits dans le musee apres avoir decoupe la cloture a l'aide d'une scie electrique. Ils avaient decroche quatre tableaux avant d'etre surpris par le declenchement de l'alarme. Contraints de fuir precipitamment, ils avaient abandonne deux œuvres dans le jardin et emporte les deux autres. Sur place, les voleurs avaient abandonne une housse portant des traces ADN. « Cette housse va nous permettre de faire des avancees significatives dans les investigations », a explique le procureur de Marseille, Nicolas Bessone, le 12 octobre. Les analyses ont permis d'identifier un suspect de 29 ans, deja vise par une enquete pour trafic de stupefiants. Deux tableaux caches sous un escalier La voiture de ce suspect faisait deja l'objet d'une surveillance policiere. Son suivi, complete par des donnees de geolocalisation, a conduit les enqueteurs jusqu'a la maison d'un autre homme a Clermont-l'Herault, ou les tableaux etaient caches derriere un faux mur, sous un escalier. Six personnes ont ete interpellees et quatre hommes mis en examen, notamment pour vol en bande organisee ou recel. Les enqueteurs soupconnaient egalement la preparation d'un autre cambriolage apres la visite d'un suspect a la Fondation Maeght, qui abrite une importante collection d'art moderne. Des œuvres endommagees et une securite en question Retrouvees plus d'un mois apres leur disparition, les deux peintures ne sont pas intactes. Portrait de Madame Colonna Romano presente une dechirure, tandis que le cadre de Jeune femme au puits a ete abîme. Les œuvres ont ete transferees a Marseille pour y etre examinees et, si necessaire, restaurees avant leur retour au musee. Ce vol relance les inquietudes autour de la protection du patrimoine francais. Le musee Renoir occupe la derniere demeure du peintre, et les deux tableaux retrouves font partie des œuvres recuperees apres la Seconde Guerre mondiale, aujourd'hui conservees par l'etat. Leur disparition s'ajoute a plusieurs vols retentissants commis dans des musees francais, notamment celui des bijoux de la Couronne au Louvre en 2025 .

items.title: Pope’s cancer operation already reshaping papacy
items.description: With Pope Leo XIV recovering in hospital on Thursday following his lung cancer operation, questions are swirling about how the illness could change his papacy, less than two years after his election. The 71-year-old leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics had a part of his lung removed on Tuesday and is undergoing further tests to determine if he is cancer-free or needs further treatment. In the meantime, the Chicago-born pontiff is expected to spend at least a few days recovering at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome. He was out of bed after a “good night”, the Vatican said on Thursday, and sources said the pope is upbeat. But experts said the unexpected diagnosis will fundamentally change the papacy in some ways. “Illness acts as a crossroads in a pontificate — it either accelerates its momentum or diminishes its power,” Vatican watcher Giacomo Galeazzi wrote in La Stampa daily on Thursday. Mikael Corre, Vatican correspondent for France’s La Croix newspaper, told AFP the way Leo is perceived has shifted. “No-one expected to be waiting for medical bulletins again so soon — certainly not with this particular pope, who was 69 at the time of the conclave” in which he was elected, he said. When Leo’s predecessor, Pope Francis, spent more than five weeks in hospital in early 2025, the Vatican began issuing regular medical bulletins detailing the pope’s medical treatment and the critical episodes when his life was in danger. In May 2025, tennis-mad Leo — a keen gym-goer — became the youngest man chosen to lead the Church since John Paul II almost 40 years earlier. “He was the ‘athletic pope’ who also proved to be a great traveller. “He may remain both but he will now also be a pope whose health is constantly scrutinised,” Corre said. – ‘Prudent’ – Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20 and his near-term travel plans are uncertain, including a demanding scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17. He is expected initially to have a scaled-back schedule, with fewer commitments and fewer public engagements. “I think he is going to want to jump right back into things as much as he can. I think he’ll push himself,” said US Vatican expert Elise Ann Allen, who has written a biography of the pope. “But he’s also very prudent. Leo understands his limitations and he’ll listen to them,” she told AFP. The world’s first American pope has gradually imprinted his style on the Church leadership, speaking out on some of the world’s most pressing issues, from conflicts to artificial intelligence. He has also proved unafraid to criticise world leaders or defend himself against US President Donald Trump’s attacks. “We’re not going to see him change his style,” Allen said. “Scares like this have a way of crystallising things for you, of what’s important,” she said. “He will be even more determined, I think.” – ‘Shift priorities’ – Some Vatican insiders think Leo’s illness might “shift his priorities”, meaning fewer trips and more appointments, Corre said. Several appointments are expected soon, in any case. Leo has yet to create any cardinals, the red-hatted Princes of the Church who will vote in the conclave to elect his successor. Five heads of dicasteries — Vatican departments — have also reached retirement age but have yet to be replaced. Leo inherited a divided Church, with liberal and conservative factions that bickered under his predecessor Francis. While he has been tasked with overcoming such polarisation, there are those inside the Vatican who hope Leo’s illness will spur him into replacing close allies of Francis in key dicasteries with more conservative figures, Corre said. Others expect him to forge ahead instead with diplomatic efforts, which have already “brought great stability”, Allen said. “I think this health crisis has eased those frictions even further,” she said. “It’s brought the Catholic Church together in support around Pope Leo in a very strong way,” she said. items.title: List of Champions League top scorers after Matchday 2
items.description: Erling Haaland, Ermedin Demirović and Nicolò Tresoldi are joint top scorers in the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League after Matchday 2, with four goals each. According to UEFA, the trio lead the scoring chart following the conclusion of the second round of league-phase fixtures on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. Five players are immediately behind them with three goals apiece. Tresoldi, who plays for Club Brugge, made a major move up the rankings after scoring a hat-trick in his side’s thrilling 4-3 victory over Inter Milan on Tuesday, October 13. The forward had previously scored a penalty in Club Brugge’s Matchday 1 defeat to Aston Villa. Manchester City striker Haaland joined him on four goals after scoring twice in his team’s 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday. The Norwegian has scored all four of City’s goals in the competition so far. Stuttgart forward Demirović also reached four goals after scoring in his team’s 3-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava. He had opened his Champions League campaign with a hat-trick against Viking in September. Liverpool’s Bradley Barcola, Paris Saint-Germain duo Ousmane Dembélé and Ferran Torres, Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Aston Villa forward Nicolas Jackson are next on the list with three goals each. Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool’s 6-3 victory over LASK, while Kane netted twice in Bayern Munich’s 3-3 draw against Viking. Jackson also scored twice as Aston Villa defeated Fenerbahçe 6-0. The results leave a closely contested race for the Champions League Golden Boot, with several established forwards and emerging talents already making their mark early in the league phase. items.title: CIMG awards drive competition among Ghanaian businesses
items.description: The Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), says its annual marketing awards have encouraged businesses to rethink how they attract customers, build brands and compete in the market over the past 36 years. The Institute says the awards have promoted better marketing practices and pushed organisations to find more innovative ways to improve performance. The awards were established to raise the profile of marketing in Ghana and recognise individuals and companies whose work demonstrates excellence in the profession. Over the years, the CIMG award has expanded to cover several sectors of the economy, including banking, insurance, manufacturing, telecommunications, hospitality and the media. Recognising businesses and individuals The CIMG National Marketing Performance Awards cover six main areas: personalities, the Hall of Fame, media and marketing communications, business organisations, products and not-for-profit organisations. Individual awards include Marketing Man of the Year, Marketing Woman of the Year, Marketing Practitioner of the Year and Marketing Student of the Year. Companies compete in categories covering industries such as banking, insurance, agriculture, healthcare, retail, e-commerce and telecommunications. The awards also recognise marketing campaigns on television, radio, outdoor and digital platforms. The awards reward consistency and individual achievement. Companies that win in a category for three consecutive years qualify for induction into the CIMG Hall of Fame on their fourth win. Those that maintain their Hall of Fame status for ten consecutive years qualify for induction into the Elite Hall of Fame on their 11th win. They must, however, continue to meet the Institute’s assessment requirements to retain their status. How winners are selected The selection process has changed considerably since the awards were introduced. CIMG initially relied on committees that visited companies and individuals to assess their performance. The process later moved to formal presentations by shortlisted nominees. Today, nominees complete detailed questionnaires, which independent evaluators assess before the results go to the CIMG Governing Council for a final decision. The assessment considers factors such as customer understanding, innovation, market reach, corporate reputation, social impact and contribution to national development. According to the Institute, the assessment panels comprise 60 per cent technical professionals and 40 per cent non-technical members with the competence to evaluate the submissions. Maverick Research and Media Monitoring Services worked with CIMG to collate and assess the results for this year’s awards. Keeping pace with business changes The awards have also evolved to reflect changes in the business environment. New categories introduced over the years have brought areas such as e-commerce, digital media, real estate, private healthcare and courier services into the competition. CIMG has also moved its nomination and assessment processes online, allowing nominees to submit questionnaires digitally and panel members to evaluate entries through the same system. The Institute says it will continue reviewing the criteria to keep the awards relevant to changing business needs and public expectations. Its regulatory responsibilities are supported by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana Act, 2020 (Act 1021), and the 2023 Regulations (L.I. 2479). For CIMG, the challenge is to maintain confidence in the awards while encouraging businesses to take marketing seriously – not simply as a way to sell products, but as a means of understanding customers, improving services and building lasting relationships.

items.title: 2027: APC targets two million votes for Tinubu in Jigawa
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has pledged to deliver two million votes to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, saying it expects to surpass the votes recorded by former President Muhammadu Buhari in the state. The Commissioner for Special Duties and Humanitarian Affairs, Auwalu D. Sankara, made the declaration while addressing supporters at a one-million-man march in Dutse in support of the re-election bids of Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi. Sankara said the turnout at the rally demonstrated the APC’s strength in Jigawa, adding that the party was confident of securing overwhelming support in the 2027 elections. He attributed the party’s growing support in the state to what he described as the people-oriented policies and leadership of Tinubu and Namadi. According to him, Buhari secured 794,738 votes, representing 71.84 per cent of the total votes cast in Jigawa during the 2019 presidential election. He expressed confidence that Tinubu would surpass the figure in 2027, claiming that the APC had gained ground as opposition members defected to the ruling party. “Despite the popularity of the late President Muhammadu Buhari, he secured 794,738 votes in Jigawa during the 2019 presidential election because of the influence of opposition parties,” Sankara said. “Today, most of those opposition parties have been swallowed by the APC because of its good policies and people-oriented programmes. “I am confident that we will double the votes Buhari received and deliver about two million votes to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.” The commissioner urged residents to disregard what he described as misleading statements by opposition politicians ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also expressed optimism that Tinubu would receive massive support from Jigawa voters, insisting that the President was committed to improving the welfare of Nigerians. Also speaking, the chairman of the movement, Salihu Atafi, said the Tinubu and Namadi administrations had recorded achievements in various sectors in less than three years. “Mr President has made a significant impact on the lives of Nigerians, including through infrastructure development, youth and women’s empowerment, and improved security in some parts of the country,” Atafi said. He urged youths to sustain their mobilisation efforts and work towards delivering the votes pledged to the APC candidates in 2027. items.title: Photo du jour | La tombe du martyr de Bizerte
items.description: Cette photo réalisée par un photographe français (Cliché Vaguer) dans les années soixante au cimetière musulman de Ferryville, actuelle Menzel Bourguiba, représente deux fillettes devant la tombe d’un martyr tombé lors de la guerre de Bizerte, en 1961. Nous remercions notre collègue et collaborateur Abdellatif Ben Salem qui nous l’a envoyée. Il l’avait trouvée, il y a quelques années, chez un antiquaire parisien et l’avait achetée pour sa valeur historique. Le martyr dont la tombe est sur la photo s’appelle Mokhtar Ben Amor Ayari, né le 6 novembre 1934 et décédé sous les balles des soldats français le 19 juillet 1961. Il avait 27 ans et avait répondu à l’appel du devoir, comme des centaines d'autres martyrs tunisiens de cette guerre qui aurait pu être évitée si les responsables tunisiens et français de l'époque avaient fait parler non pas leurs ressentiments mais leur raison. items.title: Teacher, 32 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
items.description: PESHAWAR: At least 33 people, including 32 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday. Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33 from an earlier figure of 28. The deceased included 32 students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher, he said. A total of 20 injured children were also brought to the hospital, most of whom have since been discharged. Three children who sustained serious head injuries remained under treatment, he added. Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP A spokesman for Rewscue 1122 said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way. “When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said. Speaking to Geo News , Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded. “Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said. Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement. Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred. A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak. “Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying. A girl who was injured after a school roof collapse receives first aid at a hospital in Peshawar October 15, 2026. —AFP Speaking to Dawn , Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight. “I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said. “When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added. Resident Sohail told AFP “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said. Volunteers and relatives shift the body of a victim, killed after a roof collapsed at a school, into an ambulance outside a hospital in Peshawar on October 15, 2026. —AFP KP governor orders audit Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse. “The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities. In another statement on his X account, the KP governor added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to “identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary”. “We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Kundi wrote. Meanwhile, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report on Thursday. The committee included: Javid Iqbal, the chairman of the Private Schools Regularity Authority; Muhammad Farooq, the deputy secretary of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department; and a member to be co-opted by a committee. The committee was tasked with probing the incident and ascertaining the facts that led to the roof collapse, unearthing the factors that led to it, suggesting measures to prevent such incidents in the future and making appropriate recommendations. Separately, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed ordered Peshawar CCPO to oversee the rescue operation and directed the traffic police to establish a “green corridor” to ensure uninterrupted movement of ambulances. Rescue and police teams were directed to utilise all available resources, a statement said. “In this hour of grief, KP police stands with the affected families,” the IGP was quoted as saying. Residents and rescue workers gather near an ambulance after a school roof collapse in Peshawar Pakistan on October 15.—Reuters PM Shehbaz takes ‘serious notice’ Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken “serious notice” of the incident, as he offered his condolences to the bereaved families in a post on X. “Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country,” DPM Dar said. He added that “ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount”. “All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.” PM Shehbaz also phone the KP governor according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The prime minister offered condolences to the families of the deceased and directed authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to the injured and all possible assistance to the affected families, the statement said. The prime minister also sought a comprehensive report on the incident. The governor briefed the prime minister on the incident and informed him that the school owner had been arrested and an investigation into the incident had been launched. The prime minister directed that all aspects of the incident be examined and action be taken against those responsible in accordance with the law, the statement added. People gather to identify their loved ones who were killed after a school roof collapse, at a hospital in Peshawar, October 15, 2026.—AFP Condolences President Asif Ali Zardari also expressed “profound shock and grief” over the tragic school incident in a statement on X. “This heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock,” he said, extending his condolences to the families of the children killed. He directed relevant authorities to provide top-notch medical facilities to the injured and extend assistance to the affected families. “In this hour of sorrow, the entire nation shares equally in the grief of the affected families,” he said. President Zardari emphasised the need for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the incident and to ensure that all educational institutions’ buildings were following safety standards. PM Shehbaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the incident, in a statement shared by his office. He extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured, directing that “all possible medical assistance” be provided. PM Shehbaz has also issued instructions to expedite relief operations, the statement said. In a post on X, he said: “My heart is with the families grieving the loss of their children and a teacher in the tragic roof collapse at a school in Peshawar. No parent should have to endure such pain. I extend my deepest condolences and pray for strength for every family affected.” He said that he had directed that the injured receive the best possible care. “We will ensure a thorough investigation into this tragedy and take every necessary step to protect the safety of children in schools across the country,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed grief over the incident. In a post on X, he said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy, adding that the thought of parents sending their children to school in the morning only to receive news of their deaths was heartbreaking. He expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. Bilawal’s sister, MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari, also extended condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured. She said schools must be places of learning and protection, adding that those responsible for ensuring children’s safety must be held accountable. Unicef also expressed its deep sadness over the incident. Unicef representative in Pakistan, Pernille Ironside, said in a statement: “Unicef extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities affected by this devastating incident.” “Our thoughts are also with the injured children; we wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said. Unicef called for urgent action to ensure that all schools, public and private, meet building safety standards and undergo regular safety inspections. “These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in future,” Ironside said. “Every child has the right to learn in a safe environment, where children can learn, grow and thrive, protected from harm. Going to school should never put a child’s life at risk,” she said. People stand near rubble after a school roof collapse in Peshawar, October 15, 2026. —Reuters Roof collapse incidents Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. In July, three girls, aged 3 to 13, were killed after a portion of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed and the rubble fell on them. The same month, a child died, and at least five other people were injured after the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood . On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. The incident had come less than two months after four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed. A probe into the DG Khan incident revealed that construction for an extension of the tuition centre’s building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed. Last week, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm. In June, a labourer was killed, and three others were injured when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed in Khawaspur locality of Lalamusa , Gujrat. The same month, two people were injured after the roof of a house collapsed in Lahore’s Nishtar area. In August, a couple was killed, and their daughters were injured after the roof of their house in Shahzad Town , Islamabad, collapsed following three days of heavy rainfall. Additional input from AFP

items.title: Nigeria’s image: Clarity, competence, not propaganda, will restore trust — Momoh, Peterside
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Chairman of the Advisory Board of the Nigerian Reputation Management Group (NRMG), Dr John Momoh, has said Nigeria does not need propaganda to improve its international image, but clarity in policymaking, consistency in governance and competence in service delivery. Momoh said the country’s reputation would improve when government policies were clearly communicated and public services worked effectively. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday at the inaugural Nigeria Reputation Day, themed, “Own the Narrative: Shaping Nigeria’s Reputation Together.” The Channels Television chairman said Nigerians were more interested in effective governance and tangible improvements in their lives than publicity campaigns aimed at promoting the country’s image. “Nigerians are not asking for miracles. They are asking for clarity, consistency, competence. When policy is clear and service works, reputation takes care of itself,” he said. Momoh warned against presenting an overly flattering picture of Nigeria while ignoring the challenges confronting its citizens. “Owning the narrative does not mean lying to ourselves. It does not mean polishing this country until it shines in a press statement while our people are still struggling. Nigerians are too smart for that. We see through spin,” he said. He noted that Nigeria had contrasting realities, including frustrations associated with its institutions and the resilience demonstrated by its citizens through innovation, creativity and enterprise. Citing examples of innovation and cultural influence, Momoh referenced young people using drones to deliver medicine in Enugu and the international popularity of Afrobeats. He described reputation as the cumulative effect of people’s experiences and interactions with a country rather than the outcome of a publicity campaign. “Reputation is not what we say about ourselves. It is what people feel when they deal with us. It is not a campaign with a start and end date. It is daily deposit into a trust account,” he said. Addressing private sector leaders, Momoh said their business practices and treatment of employees also influenced Nigeria’s reputation, noting that the quality of products, fair workplace practices and fulfilment of promises contributed to public trust. He urged media organisations and creative professionals to prioritise accuracy amid the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate convincing but potentially misleading content. “In an age where AI can clone a voice in 30 seconds, be first with truth, not first with rumour,” he said. Momoh also encouraged journalists to scrutinise those in power while reporting credible progress and positive developments. He urged Nigerians at home and abroad to speak honestly about the country, arguing that criticism and patriotism could coexist. “Criticise, because we must. But we can love Nigeria honestly,” he said. Also speaking at the event, former Director-General of the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), Dr Dakuku Peterside, described national reputation as a strategic asset with implications for investment, trade, tourism and international relations. Peterside said Nigeria’s size and economic significance placed it under international scrutiny, making the way the country was perceived an important consideration in its global engagements. “Every nation tells a story about itself. And every nation also lets others tell that story for it, whether it admits this or not. Nigeria is the most populous Black nation on earth, one of Africa’s largest economies. So world is watching. What matters is who shapes what it sees,” he said. He described reputation as “the invisible highway along which capital, trade and talent flow,” warning that a damaged national image could increase business costs, limit opportunities and undermine trust. According to him, a country’s reputation can influence investment decisions, the treatment of its citizens at international borders, tourism and the confidence of foreign partners. Peterside said efforts to improve Nigeria’s image must be supported by tangible achievements, effective institutions and the lived experiences of its citizens. “The strongest narrative Nigeria can project is one our actions consistently affirm and our people can confidently believe in,” he said. He argued that international portrayals of Nigeria had often focused on poverty, disorder and sensational events, overlooking other aspects of its history, cultural heritage and achievements. While acknowledging that some negative portrayals reflected genuine challenges, Peterside said they did not capture the full complexity of the country. He cited the artistic traditions of Nok terracotta and Benin bronze casting, as well as the contributions of Nigerian scholars, writers and Nobel laureates to global thought. He also referenced the continued debate over the restitution of Benin artefacts taken during the British expedition of 1897, many of which remain in overseas collections. Peterside further highlighted Nigeria’s cultural diversity, noting that its more than 250 ethnic groups continued to contribute to the country’s social, economic and cultural life. He said Nigeria needed to play a more active role in shaping how it was understood internationally, rather than attempting to silence criticism. According to him, the country’s reputation would be strengthened when its institutions, achievements and everyday realities provided credible evidence to support the image it sought to project. The post Nigeria’s image: Clarity, competence, not propaganda, will restore trust — Momoh, Peterside appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NSA regional director Emmanuel Reagan files nomination to contest NDC Ashanti Regional Organiser position
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Director of the National Service Authority (NSA), Emmanuel Fynn Reagan, has officially filed his nomination to contest the Ashanti Regional Organiser position of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), pledging to unite party members and strengthen the party’s electoral fortunes in the region. Mr Reagan, who is the current deputy regional youth organizer, made the commitment after submitting his nomination forms at the party’s regional secretariat, where he expressed confidence in the party’s ability to make significant electoral gains in a region traditionally dominated by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP). He said his ambition was to help dismantle the perception that the Ashanti Region remains an impregnable electoral stronghold of the NPP, insisting that no constituency should be considered beyond the NDC’s reach. “I promise the good delegates of the NDC that when they give me the mandate, the issue of stronghold will be a thing of the past,” Mr Reagan stated. He added that the party was poised to make significant inroads in the region, urging members not to underestimate the NDC’s chances of winning parliamentary seats currently held by the opposition. “The NDC will make a lot of inroads in the Ashanti Region, and nobody should dream that the NDC cannot win certain seats in the region,” he said. Mr Reagan emphasised that reversing the party’s electoral fortunes in the Ashanti Region would require purposeful leadership, integrity, credibility and a well-coordinated grassroots mobilisation strategy. According to him, the party needs leaders who are respected, capable and committed to strengthening its structures while building confidence among constituents ahead of future elections. He urged delegates to elect leaders who could unite the party, galvanise the grassroots and position the NDC to compete effectively across constituencies in the Ashanti Region. Mr Reagan expressed optimism that, with the right leadership and collective commitment, the NDC could expand its parliamentary representation and improve its electoral performance in the region.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS: Number of students alleging sexual abuse rises to 16
items.description: JoyNews Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni says the number of female students alleging sexual abuse by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School rose from 14 to 16 during his investigation. Speaking on Joy FM on Thursday, October 15, about his latest documentary, Manasseh said the initial information he received concerned five students. However, when he arrived at the school to investigate, the number increased to 14. Two additional students subsequently came forward, alleging similar encounters with the headmaster, bringing the total to 16. According to Manasseh, the additional accounts emerged as his investigation into the alleged abuse progressed. “Those who spoke, I have their names on record. When I went there, the number was 14; I am told two more names were added, so we have 16,” he said. His documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , examines allegations against the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. Manasseh also expressed concern about what he described as widespread awareness of the allegations within the Obuasi community, including among members of the National Democratic Congress, despite an apparent reluctance to speak publicly. items.title: Coastal highway: Wabara demands probe of N15trn project
items.description: … Accuses Tinubu govt of breaching procurement rules … Questions contract award, environmental assessment and subsequent realignment By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Former Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara, has called for a comprehensive investigation into the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project, raising concerns over alleged breaches of procurement and other statutory requirements. Wabara accused the President Bola Tinubu-led Federal Government of failing to ensure compliance with due process, transparency and accountability in the award and execution of the project. In a statement, the former Senate President questioned whether the contract had been awarded in accordance with the Public Procurement Act, 2007, and other applicable legal and regulatory requirements. He also raised concerns about the engineering design, environmental impact assessment and legislative approvals for the project, urging the relevant authorities to establish whether all necessary procedures were followed. Wabara said the controversies surrounding the proposed 750-kilometre highway had raised questions about the management of public infrastructure projects under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration. He stressed that projects of such strategic importance should be subjected to transparent procurement processes and appropriate regulatory oversight. The PDP BoT chairman argued that questions surrounding the contract award, funding and environmental assessments warranted an independent review to determine whether the project complied with established requirements. He also questioned the decision to realign sections of the highway towards existing roads, reportedly in response to climate change and other environmental concerns. According to him, the development underscored the need to examine the adequacy of the original engineering plans and environmental assessments. Wabara called for a comprehensive investigation into the conception, approval, contract award and implementation of the project, urging the relevant authorities to establish the facts and address any irregularities found. He said public infrastructure projects should remain open to scrutiny, regardless of the level of government responsible for their execution. “The secrecy, lack of public accountability and utter disregard for statutory frameworks are alarming and unacceptable in a democracy,” he said. Wabara maintained that major infrastructure projects should be executed in accordance with the law, transparent procedures and established accountability mechanisms. He also argued that the scale of public resources committed to the coastal highway made transparency essential, particularly amid the economic challenges facing Nigerians. The former Senate President said citizens were entitled to information on how contracts were awarded, how public funds were utilised and whether the necessary legal and regulatory requirements had been met. He urged the Federal Government to provide clear answers to the concerns raised and called on the relevant authorities to ensure accountability if any breaches were established. items.title: Le Maroc attend une cargaison de 40 000 tonnes de gazole russe
items.description: Une cargaison d’environ 40 000 tonnes de gazole russe à faible teneur en soufre fait route vers le Maroc, selon des données du London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). Cette expédition intervient après un assouplissement de certaines restrictions américaines sur les transactions liées aux produits pétroliers russes, alors que les prix des carburants continuent d’augmenter dans le Royaume. Le Maroc s’apprête à recevoir une nouvelle cargaison de gazole en provenance de Russie. Selon des informations publiées jeudi 15 octobre par le média marocain Hespress, un navire transportant près de 40 000 tonnes de gazole russe à faible teneur en soufre a quitté le port de Primorsk, sur la mer Baltique, à destination du Royaume. D’après les données du London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), la cargaison a été chargée mardi 13 octobre. L’identité de l’importateur, le port marocain de destination, la valeur commerciale de la livraison et sa date d’arrivée n’ont toutefois pas été précisés. Cette expédition intervient dans un contexte de reprise des exportations russes de produits pétroliers, après un assouplissement partiel de certaines restrictions. Le 10 octobre, une évolution des règles encadrant les exportations russes de gazole est entrée en vigueur, tandis que l’Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), relevant du département américain du Trésor, a délivré une autorisation concernant certaines transactions liées à la vente, au transport et à l’importation de produits russes. Des prix des carburants toujours élevés au Maroc L’arrivée annoncée de cette cargaison intervient alors que les automobilistes marocains font face à de nouvelles hausses des prix à la pompe. Au début du mois d’octobre, le litre de carburant a dépassé les 16,30 dirhams dans certaines stations-service, avec des écarts selon les villes et les réseaux de distribution. Dans ce contexte, la reprise des approvisionnements russes soulève une question centrale : dans quelle mesure les évolutions des prix internationaux et les conditions d’achat des importateurs peuvent-elles se répercuter sur les prix payés par les consommateurs marocains ? L’arrivée de cette cargaison ne signifie toutefois pas qu’une baisse des prix à la pompe est imminente. Celle-ci dépend notamment des conditions d’achat, des coûts de transport, des marges de distribution et de l’évolution des cours internationaux. Les importations russes, un précédent depuis 2023 Le Maroc avait déjà accru ses importations de gazole russe en 2023, après la réorganisation des flux pétroliers mondiaux consécutive à la guerre en Ukraine et à l’embargo européen sur les produits pétroliers russes transportés par voie maritime. En mars 2023, Nadia Fettah Alaoui, alors ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, avait indiqué que les importations marocaines de gazole russe avaient progressé de 13 % entre le 1er janvier et le 27 février de cette année-là, selon une réponse à une question parlementaire. Des données de l’Agence américaine d’information sur l’énergie (EIA), publiées en mai 2024, avaient également mis en évidence la progression des exportations russes de gazole vers plusieurs marchés africains, dont le Maroc, la Libye, la Tunisie et le Ghana. La diversification des approvisionnements en question Cette nouvelle livraison remet en lumière les enjeux de diversification des sources d’approvisionnement du Maroc en produits pétroliers. Pour les importateurs, la multiplication des fournisseurs internationaux peut offrir des possibilités de négociation et des conditions d’achat plus compétitives. Mais pour les consommateurs, l’enjeu reste celui de la répercussion effective de ces conditions sur les prix de vente. Depuis la libéralisation des prix des carburants à la fin de 2015, les tarifs à la pompe sont fixés par les opérateurs de distribution. La cargaison de 40 000 tonnes constitue ainsi un nouvel épisode dans l’évolution des circuits d’approvisionnement du Royaume. Son impact concret sur le marché marocain dépendra des conditions commerciales de cette livraison et de la manière dont les évolutions des cours internationaux seront répercutées sur les prix à la pompe. The post Le Maroc attend une cargaison de 40 000 tonnes de gazole russe appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: NIS vows justice after officer killed in Niger attack
items.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has vowed to bring the perpetrators of an attack on two of its personnel in Niger to justice, following the death of one officer and serious injury to another. The Service Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller of Immigration (DCI) Akinsola Akinlabi, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. He said the incident occurred on Oct. 6, when two personnel conducting routine surveillance were violently attacked by unidentified assailants. “Sadly, one of the officers, Assistant Superintendent of Immigration (ASI) I. U. Babangida, tragically lost his life, while the other, Insp. A. K. Musa, sustained serious injuries but managed to escape and is currently receiving medical attention. “The fallen officer has since been laid to rest in accordance with Islamic rites. The Service honours his sacrifice and unwavering commitment to duty,” he said. Akinlabi extended the Service’s condolences to the deceased officer’s family, colleagues and loved ones, while wishing the injured personnel a speedy recovery. He assured both families of the service’s continued support and assistance during this difficult period. The spokesperson added that the NIS was working with the Nigerian government and relevant security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attack and ensure they face justice. items.title: En Russie, les deux tiers des écoles participent à la propagande de guerre
items.description: Selon un rapport publié hier, mercredi 14 octobre, par le New Eurasian Strategies Centre (NEST) et réalisé par le think tank indépendant Cedar, au moins 26 000 des 40 000 écoles russes participent à la propagande de guerre. Celles-ci organisent des événements en soutien aux militaires, encouragent les élèves à écrire des lettres aux soldats au front, ou prennent part à des collectes d’aide humanitaire pour le front Оставьте детей в покое : как Кремль приучает новое поколение к войне , Cedar, 14 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Ce chiffre sous-estime vraisemblablement l’ampleur de la propagande de guerre. L’étude s’appuie principalement sur les publications des écoles sur le réseau social russe VKontakte (VK). Les établissements qui ne disposent pas de compte n’ont ainsi pas été inclus, pas plus que les écoles absentes de l’échantillon. Les activités de propagande dans les écoles russes ont évolué depuis 2022. Tandis qu’au cours de la première année de l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine, on demandait principalement aux élèves de confectionner des cadeaux et d’écrire des lettres pour les soldats au front, ces activités se sont institutionnalisées depuis, avec l’élaboration de directives méthodologiques, et font désormais place à des heures de vie de classe consacrées à la guerre, à des rencontres avec des vétérans et à des visites de musées. Depuis 2022, les écoles russes dispensent ainsi chaque semaine un cours intitulé « Conversations sur l’essentiel » ( Разговоры о важном ), qui consiste en une série de leçons « patriotiques » visant à aligner les valeurs spirituelles et morales des élèves sur la stratégie de sécurité nationale de la Fédération de Russie. À partir de la rentrée 2026, ce programme est décliné dans les maternelles sous un nouveau nom : « Jeux bienveillants » (Добрые игры). Ces séances, destinées aux enfants de 3 à 7 ans, doivent notamment leur présenter la « réunification » de la Crimée avec la Russie et définir l’héroïsme comme la « disposition à se sacrifier pour les autres » На пропагандистских занятиях дошкольникам будут рассказывать, что Крым – российский, а героизм – это самопожертвование », ЭХО , 8 septembre 2026.'> 2 . Sur le site officiel du programme, un jeu destiné aux enfants de 3-4 ans leur fait ainsi « traverser le pont de Crimée » en train, avant de rentrer à la maison en répétant : « Comme c’est bien que nous soyons un seul pays ! ». À partir de 6 ans, on leur apprend que la Crimée est une partie historique de la Russie « revenue à la maison », et on cultive chez eux un « sentiment de justice » à l’égard de cette « réunification ». Une famille contemple le pont de Crimée, présenté comme « la route de la maison ». Construit par la Russie après l’annexion de la péninsule en 2014, l’ouvrage relie selon le texte « la Crimée et la partie continentale de la Russie ». © Institut d’étude de l’enfance, de la famille et de l’éducation / Добрые игры Une guide présente à des enfants le monument aux Navires coulés de Sébastopol, avec des navires de guerre en arrière-plan. Le texte associé décrit la « ville-héros » comme « étroitement liée à l’histoire de la flotte russe ». © Institut d’étude de l’enfance, de la famille et de l’éducation / Добрые игры Une famille contemple le pont de Crimée, présenté comme « la route de la maison ». Construit par la Russie après l’annexion de la péninsule en 2014, l’ouvrage relie selon le texte « la Crimée et la partie continentale de la Russie ». © Institut d’étude de l’enfance, de la famille et de l’éducation / Добрые игры Une guide présente à des enfants le monument aux Navires coulés de Sébastopol, avec des navires de guerre en arrière-plan. Le texte associé décrit la « ville-héros » comme « étroitement liée à l’histoire de la flotte russe ». © Institut d’étude de l’enfance, de la famille et de l’éducation / Добрые игры Au-delà de l’aspect idéologique, une formation militaire a également été ajoutée au curriculum en 2023, avant de devenir en 2024 une matière hebdomadaire obligatoire à partir de 14 ans, dont la part militaire a été portée de 20 % à 50 % à la rentrée 2026. Celle-ci comprend une introduction au montage et démontage d’une kalachnikov, à la mise en place d’un gilet pare-balles, ainsi qu’un module d’étude portant sur « la guerre informationnelle et psychologique ». En 2024, une mère qui refusait d’envoyer son fils en stage militaire a été condamnée à une amende de 30 000 roubles pour « discrédit de l’armée » Я не просила учить моего ребенка нажимать на курок », Новая газета , 15 octobre 2024.'> 3 . Les données disponibles ne montrent pas de corrélation entre les pertes liées à la guerre, rapportées à la population, et l’intensité de la propagande à l’école, selon les régions. C’est toutefois dans les villes de moins de 10 000 habitants que l’on observe la plus forte concentration d’activités pro-guerre. À l’inverse, les écoles des grandes villes du pays, comme Moscou et Saint-Pétersbourg, sont moins concernées par la propagande pro-guerre. Les chiffres compilés par Mediazona et le service russe de la BBC montrent que c’est également dans les grandes villes que le nombre de morts au front en Ukraine est parmi les plus faibles : 33 pour 100 000 habitants à Moscou et 49 à Saint-Pétersbourg, contre plus de 580 en Transbaïkalie ou à Touva Потери России в войне с Украиной », Медиазона , données mises à jour le 9 octobre 2026.'> 4 . L’article En Russie, les deux tiers des écoles participent à la propagande de guerre est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: You cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates, expect votes — Obi’s media office tells Tinubu
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Peter Obi Media Office has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his decision not to accompany the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council to every campaign event ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying he cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates and expect Nigerians to renew his mandate. The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, said the President must personally defend his record in office rather than rely on political allies and party chieftains to campaign on his behalf. In a statement signed on Thursday by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri, the office argued that although political surrogates could speak for the President, they could not assume responsibility for his policies and performance. It said the President could not delegate accountability or leave political allies to defend his administration while Nigerians continued to grapple with the effects of government policies. Tinubu had said he would not accompany the APC Presidential Campaign Council to every campaign event ahead of the 2027 general elections, citing the need to prioritise governance, economic obligations and efforts to attract investors. The President made the declaration on Wednesday in Abuja while inaugurating the APC Presidential Campaign Council, urging its members to lead the party’s mobilisation efforts nationwide while he attended to matters of state. He reportedly agreed with concerns that electioneering should not interfere with his responsibilities as President, stressing that the country required his attention. Reacting, the Obi media office challenged Tinubu to explain his administration’s performance directly to Nigerians. The statement read, “President Bola Tinubu reportedly says the demands of governance may keep him away from the campaign trail. Nigerians deserve to ask: If he cannot make time to face the electorate, why should surrogates be sent to ask for their votes? “The President cannot delegate accountability. He cannot outsource the defence of his record to political allies, party chieftains, and praise singers while millions of Nigerians struggle with the consequences of his government’s policies. “Surrogates can speak for the President, but they cannot answer for his failures. They can repeat his promises, but they cannot make those promises a reality. They can campaign in his name, but they cannot carry his responsibility.” The office further challenged Tinubu to explain how the performance of his administration had affected the cost of food, transportation, electricity, housing and other necessities. “If the administration has delivered on its promises, why should the President be reluctant to defend that record before Nigerians himself? If the economy is improving, let him explain how that improvement is reflected in the cost of food, transportation, electricity, housing, and necessities. If his policies are working, let him face the citizens who want to know when the hardship will end,” it said. The statement argued that governance should not be treated as a reason to avoid public scrutiny, maintaining that a candidate seeking another term must be prepared to account for his record. “Governance is not an excuse to avoid accountability. In a democracy, governance is the very record a candidate must defend before asking for another mandate,” the office said. It added that Nigerians were being asked to assess Tinubu’s policies, promises and performance, rather than those of the political allies campaigning on his behalf. “The Nigerian people deserve a direct conversation with their President, not a relay of rehearsed talking points from political messengers,” the statement said. The office urged Tinubu to explain his administration’s achievements, address unfulfilled promises and respond to questions from Nigerians if he wanted them to renew his mandate. “A President who seeks the people’s mandate must be prepared to face the people. Surrogates may carry the message, but they cannot carry the burden of accountability,” it added. The post You cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates, expect votes — Obi’s media office tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana’s economy grows by 7.4% in July 2026
items.description: Data published by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) shows that the country recorded a year-on-year economic growth of 7.4 percent in July 2026 compared to the same period last year. This was contained in the latest Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth (MIEG) released by the GSS. Sector by sector, the data shows that Agriculture increased by 3.7 percent. The Industry sector recorded an increase of 5.4 percent. The increase was attributed to the growth observed in the mining and quarrying sub-sector. The Services sector grew by 12.2 percent. The expansion in activity was mainly driven by Information & Communication sub-sector. Explaining the data, the GSS said the services sector was the main contributor to the July 2026 7.4 percent growth. The sector contributed 63.8 percent to the overall growth of the 7.4 percent in economic activities. Industry contributed 20.5 percent while agriculture contributed 14.1 percent. Net Indirect taxes contributed 1.6 percent. Agriculture increased by 3.7 percent in the same period under review. This was driven by the crops and livestock subsector. July 2026 MIEG PPT Download

items.title: Funcas ve señales de ralentización en la economía española por la persistencia de la inflación
items.description: La Fundación de las Cajas de Ahorros (Funcas) ha actualizado este jueves sus previsiones macroeconómicas para el periodo 2026-2028, anticipando una paulatina desaceleración de la economía española que comenzará a percibirse con mayor claridad el próximo año. De esta forma, el Producto Interior Bruto (PIB) pasaría de crecer un 2,5% este año (una décima menos de lo que espera el Gobierno), a moderarse hasta el 1,8% en 2027 y el 1,7% en 2028. Este enfriamiento del ciclo económico responde principalmente al enquistamiento de las presiones inflacionistas, el incremento de los tipos de interés y que algunos sectores que han sostenido la actividad en los últimos años, como el turismo, perderán empuje. Además, el centro de análisis eleva su estimación de inflación media anual hasta el 3,7% para este año y el 3,1% para el que viene, medio punto porcentual por encima de sus anteriores cálculos. items.title: Lahore ATC extends physical remand of PTI's Hammad Azhar
items.description: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Thursday extended the physical remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar by 12 days in the Jinnah House attack case related to the May 9 riots . Sarwar Road police had booked several PTI leaders and workers on charges of attacking and vandalising Jinnah House during the protests against the arrest of former prime minister Imran Khan. ATC Judge Sardar Muhammad Akram heard the case. During the hearing, the investigating officer (IO) sought an extension in the physical remand, saying the police wanted to conduct a polygraph test on the suspect. The IO alleged that Hammad was among those who led the attack. Opposing the request for an extension in remand, defence counsel Sikandar Zulqarnain argued that the IO had changed his stance on the recovery of evidence from his client. At the previous hearing, the police had claimed that a baton and other items had been recovered. However, the IO was now saying that the items were yet to be recovered, the counsel said. He questioned what further recoveries the police wanted to make when, according to the first information report (FIR), Hammad was not present at the alleged occurrence. The counsel also questioned why the investigation had not been completed despite 37 days of physical remand. He asked the court to send his client to jail on judicial remand, arguing that further physical remand was unnecessary if the investigation had made no progress. The state prosecutor, however, argued that the FIR did not state that Hammad was absent from the scene. He said the complainant might not have seen the suspect because he could have been standing at a distance. Addressing the court, Hammad alleged that anti-terrorism laws were being used for political victimisation and added that the dignity of the court must be upheld. He alleged that the police had changed their statements, first claiming that he was not present at the scene and later saying that a baton and petrol bombs had been recovered from him. “Does anyone keep a baton and bombs for three and a half years?” he asked. Hammad maintained that he was in Bhakkar on May 9, 2023, and claimed that he had not been interrogated for even a single day during his physical remand. He asked the court to summon the complete record, including an earlier forensic examination report, saying it would bring the truth to light. After hearing arguments from both sides, the judge reserved the verdict on the remand request. Later, the judge announced the decision and extended Hammad’s physical remand by a further 12 days.

items.title: Conte interested in replacing Carrick at Manchester United – Report
items.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Antonio Conte has indicated his willingness to take over as Manchester United head coach should the club decide to part ways with Michael Carrick, according to a report by talkSPORT. The report said representatives of the Italian manager had contacted United to express his interest in the position amid growing pressure on Carrick following the club’s disappointing run of results. United are 13th in the Premier League standings, with six points from their opening six matches. A 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur was followed by a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, extending the club’s winless run to five matches. The results have intensified speculation over Carrick’s future at Old Trafford, with Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler and Julian Nagelsmann also reportedly being considered as possible candidates. Conte, a former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager, has considerable experience in English football. He also guided Napoli to the Serie A title in the 2024/25 season before leaving his position at the Italian club earlier this year. Meanwhile, United are also facing concerns over reported tensions within the dressing room following the defeat to Atletico Madrid. Argentina international Lisandro Martinez criticised the club’s hierarchy over its summer recruitment, arguing that the squad needed further reinforcements to compete at the highest level. “It was really poor, really poor,” Martinez told Amazon Prime after the defeat. He added that the performance reflected wider concerns about the club, saying he expected more from those responsible for strengthening the squad. “To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from my technical director,” Martinez said. The defender acknowledged that the players also needed to improve but maintained that squad investment was important for the team’s progress. On whether Carrick had received sufficient backing, Martinez said he believed the manager was doing his best and questioned whether changing coaches alone would address the club’s problems. “You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas?” he said. According to talkSPORT, Martinez’s comments have received support from some senior players, adding to the pressure on United’s leadership to address the team’s struggles. Conte’s reported interest presents another potential option for United if the club decides to make a change in the dugout. However, no appointment has been confirmed, and Carrick’s immediate future remains dependent on the club’s decision. The post Conte interested in replacing Carrick at Manchester United – Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 'Let facts remains facts': Naqvi says govt had 'no option' but to impose emergency, governor's rule in KP
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday urged the opposition to stick to facts when recounting the round of talks held with the government, asserting that the Centre had “no option left” but to impose emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He made the remarks during a joint session of the Parliament, which is currently discussing two resolutions on the endorsement of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, where the opposition’s PTI was in power. The Centre took the measures on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Speaking during Thursday’s joint sitting, Naqvi sought to provide a “clarification” on the allegations levelled by the opposition and maintained that the Centre “tried our best” to take the KP government on board on the issue of counterterrorism. He said the government want a meeting of the provincial apex committee to be held. “A press release had to be issued, which would state that we will fight against terrorism together. You can ask for that press release, what was written in it and what happened; everything is before you.” Naqvi, also the interior minister, recalled that some personnel were martyred in an attack “the same day”, adding that it took place in February. “We requested the CM sahib and took him to the funerals with us. That was the last day when CM KP attended the funeral of any army officer or jawaan (soldier),” he added. Naqvi stated: “I believe that you, and those we spoke to, particularly Asad Qaiser sahib as he responded on [the issue] of terrorism that day, I guarantee that even we were not thinking of the things they were speaking on.” He went on to acknowledge that all those present during the Oct 3 talks between the government and the opposition “had an absolutely clear stance [on terrorism] that we will do this for Pakistan”. Resolutions tabled The joint sitting is taking place a day after both Houses of Parliament, in separate sittings, passed resolutions endorsing the imposition of emergency in KP. According to Article 232 , if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months. During Thursday’s joint sitting, opposition members turned up carrying placards inscribed with slogans, such as “emergency na manzoor (emergency is unacceptable)”. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended part of the session, shook hands with opposition leaders of both the Senate and the NA, pictures and footage showed. At the outset of the proceedings, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry presented a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules 1973 to suspend certain sub-rules so he could move the resolutions. As loud noes echoed and opposition members chanted “emergency na manzoor ”, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq again put the motion to a vote by asking the members to stand up, which was then adopted with 214-56 votes. Subsequently, Chaudhry moved two resolutions before the joint sitting — one for the Proclamation of Emergency under Article 232 and the second for the proclamation of governor’s rule under Article 234. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar then opened the discussion on the two resolutions. Noting that a resolution regarding the imposition of emergency also required to be passed by a joint sitting, Tarar said a special mechanism has been put in place in KP to run its affairs during the emergency and governor’s rule. He said members of the treasury benches were ready to reply to any query raised by the opposition. The law minister highlighted that the PTI-led government in KP, which now stands non-functional, was advised time and again to tackle terrorism. He again lamented that PTI leaders did not attend any funeral of martyrs who lost their lives in terrorist attacks. Tarar went on to stress that governor’s rule was imposed under Article 234, which allows the move if any provincial government was being run against the Constitution. Explaining the constitutional process to approve the resolution for emergency, he said the joint sitting could reject it by a total majority, ie 51 per cent. Similarly, the resolution for governor’s rule also required a total majority of votes for approval. At the outset of the sitting, the Parliament offered prayers for the lives lost, mostly of children, in a roof collapse in Peshawar. Gohar objects to allegations of ‘backing terrorists’ Speaking on the Parliament’s floor, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the country was going through a “very fragile situation”. He lamented that the KP government was accused of “backing terrorists”. “The prime minister has alleged that we are supporting terrorists. We are disappointed to hear that. You have to apologise to the entire population of KP and us,” he said. “Prime minister, you have given a message to the entire world that one of the federating units of the country was backing terrorists,“ Gohar added. He highlighted that the opposition stood with the government during a war with India. “But today we are called supporters of terrorists,” he regretted. Barrister Gohar rejected the proclamation of emergency and declared that the PTI will make the country stronger and eradicate terrorism when it comes into power again. He also rejected the government’s claims that PTI leaders did not attend funerals of martyrs, recalling that he himself had attended multiple funerals in KP. Gohar said the PTI was willing to engage in dialogue with the government provided that its demands were met. He lamented that speeches of opposition members were not shown in the media. Achakzai blames ‘faulty decisions’ Speaking in the Parliament, NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai blamed “faulty decisions” of the country’s rulers for the current situation. He enquired about the whereabouts of Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional and was reported to be in preventative custody . Achakzai, who leads the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), accused PML-N’s Sadiq of not running the house judiciously as the speaker. He said the opposition was ready for dialogue on issues such as empowerment of Parliament and eradicating terrorism of all kinds. “If you hold dialogue on these issues, we will give unconditional support,” he added. The opposition leader compared the KP imbroglio to the 1971 separation of East Pakistan, noting that Afridi was called a “terrorist”. “Were multiple attacks on the heads of different political parties in the past in KP committed by Sohail Afridi?” he asked. Achakzai said terrorism was introduced by those who had brought fighters for the Soviet-Afghan war. “When the Afghan war was over, these terrorists were left free in the tribal areas of the country and they started killing Pakistanis,” he added. The opposition leader then mentioned the reported deaths during the July unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). The TTAP chief sought meetings of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan with his family, friends and party workers. He questioned who had “sent” ex-premier Nawaz Sharif to exile in Saudi Arabia and who “murdered” ex-PM Benazir Bhutto. The NA speaker took exception to Achakzai’s remarks on his chairing of the session. “You are saying to me that I am not running the House correctly. You have not read Rule 30. Someone takes their mobile phone; someone disrupts [the proceedings].” Sadiq further said recordings of members’ speeches that were “anti-state” would not be uploaded on the NA’s social media accounts. Meanwhile, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas accused the government’s delegation of derailing the dialogue with the opposition, including the Oct 3 talks . The Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief said some more time should have been allowed to make the talks successful and called for resolving the public’s issues instead of blaming each other. The senator contended that people voted for the PTI in large numbers during the February 2024 general elections in reaction to Imran’s imprisonment. Noting that this was his first tenure as a parliament member, Abbas said he realised that the Constitution was a safeguard of the rights of people. He further claimed he did not receive a salary or any perks and privileges from the Senate. ‘We kept waiting’: PPP’s Rehman recounts Oct 3 talks In her remarks, PPP Senator Sherry Rehman asked the PTI to define its agenda and reasons for its long march , which the party had announced to stage towards Islamabad but remained within KP. Rehman added that President Asif Ali Zardari and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had insisted on resolving issues through dialogue because terrorism was a red line for them. She called on the opposition not to dictate to the government and to avoid giving lectures on patriotism. Rehman emphasised that everyone was trying to find common ground and “a path of action”. The PPP leader objected to the opposition’s claims that the government delegation left the Oct 3 talks. “We kept waiting for you. The speaker and I ordered food for you as leaving was not being considered. We could have sat till 5am or 6am,” she said. Rehman asserted, “We had said we would wait further […] This is not fair to say that we said ‘we are leaving’. Definitely not. Opposite.” Speaking on the topic, the NA speaker — who chaired the talks — also remarked, “What was the hurry in launching the long march?” Sadiq referred to a post on X made by Afridi about going ahead with the long march even as the negotiations were underway. “You said to ignore it, so we kept ignoring it till 3am, so I think, if you want to sit again [at the table] then do not go into further details. Those things took place in confidence; bury them here.” The PPP vice president remarked that the country faced several emergencies, including those regarding education and poverty, that needed to be seen holistically. “If you think PPP is going to support any sort of emergency which is against the Constitution, you are wrong,” she declared. “This Constitution has bound the country together through difficult times. We remember the lessons from the fall of Dhaka,” she said. “PPP has seen many phases of the path towards democracy. It (martial law) was a dark chapter in history; we do not want the country to go through such an experience again,” Rehman said, recalling “sacrifices” made by her party. JUI-F says no ‘evidence’ presented Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), who had earlier submitted a resolution opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, contended that no documentary evidence was presented before the Parliament for the decision. He argued that the proclamation under Article 234 required a report from the KP governor, but in this case, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had not presented a report explaining why governor’s rule was necessary. The JUI-F senator said the security situation in Balochistan was also grave and pointed out that a provincial government now had its writ in the Katcha areas without an emergency being imposed there. Murtaza stressed that free and transparent elections under a fair election commission were the only solution to the existing problems.
